description: Osmium is a hard, brittle, bluish-white transition metal in the platinum group with the highest density of any stable element. It is a chemical element with symbol Os and atomic number 76, and has one of the lowest abundances in the Earth's crust.
uses: Manufacturers use alloys of osmium with platinum, iridium, and other platinum-group metals for fountain pen nib tipping, electrical contacts, and other applications that require extreme durability and hardness. Osmium was also an early successful catalyst in the Haber process for nitrogen fixation.
characteristics: Osmium is a hard, brittle, blue-gray metal that is about twice as dense as lead, with a density of 22.587 g/cm³ at 20 °C. It has very high hardness at 4 GPa and an extremely high bulk modulus between 395 and 462 GPa, rivaling diamond. The metal has a very low vapor pressure and the fourth highest melting point of all elements, remains lustrous at high temperatures, and forms compounds with oxidation states ranging from −2 to +8.
